comments.quote: How does artefacto speak HTTPS and read a .tar.xz? It has never made an outbound

replies.text:
You already solved this in loadout, and the answer is option (d) — axoupdater, cargo-dist's own updater crate. I read `load`'s source to be sure.

loadout has `axoupdater = { version = "0.10", features = ["blocking"] }` and `src/update.rs` wraps it: `AxoUpdater::new_for("loadout")`, `load_receipt()`, `is_update_needed_sync()`, `run_sync()`. That one crate does the whole job — finds the receipt, picks the target triple, downloads the .tar.xz, verifies the checksum, unpacks it, and replaces the running binary. Every hard task in my `p-fetch` phase disappears.

It also already answers three other things I was asking you:

- **No receipt means no update.** loadout returns `NotManaged` and prints the installer command instead. That is exactly the "no button for those people" you just approved.
- **The check never blocks anything.** This is the part I would not have thought of. The nudge reads only a cache file on disk. When the verdict is stale it spawns a *detached child* — `load update --refresh-cache` — that does the network call and writes the answer for the *next* command. So no timeout to tune, no thread that can hang, and a new release shows up at most one command late. It stamps the cache before spawning so a burst of commands starts one child, not a swarm.
- **The cache carries the binary's version**, so a verdict computed by the old binary cannot nudge the new one that replaced it.

So I am rewriting this as revision 3: drop the hand-rolled download, extract, checksum, smoke-test and swap entirely, wrap axoupdater the way loadout does, and keep only what is genuinely artefacto's own — the page notice, the button, and the fact that a running review server keeps its old binary.

The one place I will not copy loadout exactly: loadout nudges on a TTY, artefacto nudges in the page. So the daemon still needs to read the verdict cache and put it in the state payload, and the detached-refresher trick replaces my "daily check on the tick loop".

The cost is the dependency tree — axoupdater pulls axoasset, miette, reqwest and self-replace. Bigger than the ~2-4 MB I quoted for option (a). You already pay it in loadout, so I am taking that as settled, but say the word if artefacto's binary size matters more than loadout's does.
